replies.text:
I'll analyze EVAL-08 for security threats using STRIDE methodology.

**Analysis of the design:**
This is a referral credit system where users get codes to share, and both parties receive $10 when a new account signs up. The critical security gap is that sign-up "only needs an email address" with no verification mentioned, combined with monetary credits being awarded.

**Key attack vectors:**
- Automated fake account creation for credit farming
- No email verification or fraud detection
- Missing rate limits and caps
- Potential code enumeration

Building and submitting the threat model now...

      "cwe": ["CWE-204"],

        "title": "Prevent user enumeration through referral codes",
        "given": "someone enters a referral code",
        "when": "the code is invalid",
        "then": "the response timing and message must not reveal whether the code exists"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Weak referral code generation enables prediction",
      "scenario": "If referral codes use sequential numbers or weak randomness, attacker could predict valid codes without having them shared, using credits belonging to legitimate users or generating codes for accounts that don't exist yet",
      "component": "Referral Service",
      "likelihood": 3,

      "evidence": [

      "cwe": ["CWE-330"],

      "requirement": {
        "title": "Generate unpredictable referral codes",
        "given": "a new user account is created",
        "when": "the system generates a referral code",
        "then": "the code must use cryptographically strong randomness with sufficient entropy to prevent guessing"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "Missing audit trail for referral credit attribution",
      "scenario": "When fraudulent credits are discovered, investigators cannot determine which accounts were involved, what IP addresses were used, or when the abuse occurred, making it impossible to reverse fraudulent credits or identify patterns",
      "component": "Credit System",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "evidence": [

      "asvs": ["V7.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "No logs exist to track who referred whom and when credits were given",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Log all referral credit transactions",
        "given": "referral credits are awarded",
        "when": "the transaction occurs",
        "then": "system must log referrer ID, referee ID, timestamp, IP addresses, device info, and credit amounts immutably"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Self-referral not prevented in registration flow",
      "scenario": "Attacker discovers they can use their own referral code when creating a second account, earning credits by referring themselves, then repeats this by creating chains of self-referrals across multiple accounts",
      "component": "User Registration",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 2,
      "evidence": [
        {"quote": "Each user gets a referral code. When a new account signs up with the code, both accounts receive $10 credit"}
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-863"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could use their own referral code to give themselves credits",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Block self-referrals and circular chains",
        "given": "a new account is created with a referral code",
        "when": "the system validates the referral",
        "then": "it must reject codes from the same user (email, device, IP) and detect circular referral chains"
      }
    }
  ]
}
